transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Your Name]. Um, well, I guess the main thing is I just get pulled off track by every little sound or thought. Like, I’ll be trying to work on a job application—which is a whole other thing, honestly, because I've been looking for work since my last job ended. It was at this warehouse, and the manager there was just so intense about the schedule, you know? Like, if you were two minutes late, he'd make this huge deal out of it. But anyway, yeah, I'll be trying to fill out an application and then a car drives by outside, or my phone buzzes, or I just have some random idea about, I don't know, a movie I saw last week, and suddenly I'm doing something completely different before I even notice I stopped working on the application.
Have you noticed any days where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, especially around the time you lost your job?

Down or hopeless? Um, no, not really. I mean, getting let go sucked, obviously, but I wasn't, like, crying in bed or anything. Honestly, it kind of just gave me more time to catch up on stuff I actually like doing. 

Like, I finally started playing that *Red Dead* game everyone was talking about a few years ago. The map on that thing is just huge. You can literally just ride a horse around for hours and fish, which sounds so boring, but the way the water looks is actually really realistic. I spent like three hours on Tuesday just trying to catch this one specific fish up in the snowy area of the map, and then my controller died because I always forget to plug it in. I have this really bad habit of leaving the charging cord all the way across the room on my dresser, and by the time the low battery warning flashes, I'm just too hyper-focused on the game to get up. 

But, wait, what did you ask me? Something about the warehouse job?

Do you often find yourself acting without thinking, or struggling to wait your turn in situations—like interrupting others, blurting out answers, or feeling restless when you need to stay seated for a long time?

Oh, yeah, the interrupting thing. I do that a lot. I cut people off constantly, actually. Especially my mom, or the career counselor I've been seeing. It’s just... an answer or a thought pops into my head and I just say it out loud before they’re even close to done talking. 

My mom gets so mad about it. Like, just the other day she was trying to tell me about her new blender. She bought one of those really expensive Ninja ones, you know? And she’s been making these green smoothies every single morning. They look exactly like swamp water. I tried a sip on Monday and it tasted like straight-up lawn clippings and dirt. I really don't get why people drink that stuff when you can just eat a normal meal. Like, just eat a regular apple, it's way cheaper and you don't have to clean a blender afterward. Cleaning those blades is so dangerous, anyway. But yeah, she was going on and on about the warranty on the blender, and I just blurted out something about my car insurance because I suddenly remembered my bill was due and I needed to borrow twenty bucks. The thought just comes out before I can stop it. 

Wait, did you ask something else just now? Something about waiting in line?
Do you also find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations in other parts of your life, like when you're at home, with friends, or running errands?

Yeah, it's pretty much everywhere, honestly. Like, if I'm at home trying to fix something... my buddy gave me this old lawnmower that wasn't running right, and I thought, you know, I could probably just clean the carburetor and get it going. So I pulled up this YouTube video on how to do it. The guy in the video had this really cool setup in his garage, like all these pegboards with the tools perfectly outlined in marker. I always wanted to do that, but I know I'd just lose the markers or never actually put the tools back in the right spot. My dad used to have a garage like that, and he'd get so furious if you even moved a wrench an inch to the left. But anyway, I can start watching a repair video like that, or reading the manual for a tool, but after a few minutes I realize I’ve just been staring at the screen. Like, my eyes are on it, but none of it stuck. I have to rewind it like four times just to figure out which screw he took out first. 

Oh, and running errands is the worst. I went to the hardware store for spark plugs yesterday and ended up looking at the barbecue grills for twenty minutes because they had one of those big smoker ones on display. Do people really smoke meat for like, fourteen hours? That just seems like a huge commitment for a brisket. Wait, what did you ask me about? Friends?
Looking back, did you have similar issues with staying focused or interrupting others when you were a kid, like in school or at home?

Yeah, it was exactly the same back then. Even in elementary school, my teachers were constantly moving my seat because I'd just talk out of turn all the time. I remember in fourth grade, Mrs. Gable—she was this really strict lady who always wore these enormous knit sweaters—she moved my desk right next to her big wooden filing cabinet. That cabinet always smelled like old paper and peppermint. She kept a bowl of peppermints on her desk, actually, those red and white striped ones wrapped in the crinkly plastic. I hate peppermint, to be honest. It just tastes like toothpaste. Why would anyone want candy that tastes like brushing your teeth? You're supposed to eat candy to avoid doing healthy stuff, you know? 

But yeah, she moved me because I wouldn't stop interrupting. And I was terrible with homework, too, just always forgetting it. Or if we had worksheets in class, I’d just rush right through them and make all these careless mistakes. I just wanted to get done so I could go out to recess. We played wall-ball every single day, and if you didn't get out to the blacktop fast enough, the fifth graders would take all the good bouncy red balls and leave you with the flat yellow ones that barely even bounced. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my parents or something?
Outside of what you’ve already mentioned, do you ever find yourself forgetting daily activities, losing things often, or feeling like you just can’t sit still for very long?

Yeah, I forget stuff all the time. Just regular, everyday things. Like, I never text people back. My phone is basically a graveyard of unread messages. And appointments? Forget about it. I'm always late, or I just completely space them. Like with my vocational counselor, she's always telling me to bring these specific papers, like my resume or this interest survey thing, and I swear I put them by the door, but then I get there and my hands are empty. 

She has this office downtown, right above a bakery. And man, the smell of fresh bread when you walk in the building is just unbelievable. It makes me so hungry every time I go. I usually end up buying a croissant afterward. They have these almond ones that are just covered in powdered sugar. You take one bite and it gets all over your shirt, like you've been rolling around in snow. I tried to dust it off my black hoodie last week and it just smeared everywhere, made me look like I had dandruff all over my chest. I had to go to the bathroom and try to wipe it off with a wet paper towel, but you know how cheap paper towels just disintegrate? It left all these little white fuzzies on my shirt instead. 

Wait, what was the question? Losing things?
Has this difficulty with staying focused, acting impulsively, or forgetting things caused you any problems at work, in your relationships, or in other important parts of your life?

Yeah, it definitely causes problems. Like, I've been trying to get into this program to become an automotive technician, right? Because I know I can do the hands-on stuff. I'm actually really good with cars when I'm just under the hood. But the whole process to get in... I've missed training deadlines, and I've had to redo my applications so many times that I'm basically just stuck. I'm not moving forward at all. 

It's so frustrating because the application portal they use is just terrible. It's one of those websites where if you click the back button, it deletes everything you just typed. Who even designs a website like that anymore? It feels like it was built in 1998. Speaking of 1998, my buddy has this '98 Honda Civic that he’s trying to mod, and he bought this cheap aftermarket spoiler online. We spent like three hours trying to bolt it on last weekend, but the holes didn't line up at all. We ended up having to drill new ones into his trunk lid, and I think we might have nicked the wiring for the brake lights because now they flicker every time he hits a bump. It looks so ridiculous, honestly, like a shopping cart. 

But yeah, I’m just... I'm not getting anywhere with the technician stuff because I keep messing up the paperwork and missing the dates. Wait, did you ask about my relationships too?
Do your difficulties with focus, impulsivity, or forgetfulness happen in different places, like at home, at work, or in public places, or are they limited to just one setting?

Yeah, it's pretty much everywhere. It's not just when I'm trying to do the application stuff or at home. Even when I'm just out, like at the grocery store or hanging out with friends, I can't stay focused. Like the other day, I was at the supermarket to get literally three things—milk, eggs, and bread. Simple, right? But then they had this huge display of those new energy drinks, the ones with the neon cans? 

I grabbed one because it was bright green and said it tasted like sour apple. I love sour apple stuff. Have you ever had those sour apple lollipops with the caramel on the outside? They used to give those out at Halloween all the time when I was a kid. I remember trading all my chocolate for them because I hated chocolate back then. My brother thought I was crazy, but he'd trade me, like, three mini candy bars for one lollipop. He was such a scammer, honestly. He still is, actually. He just bought this used motorcycle off some guy on the internet and didn't even check the title. Now he's dealing with all this DMV nightmare stuff. The DMV is the worst place on earth, I swear. The fluorescent lights alone give me a headache. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Was it about where I have trouble focusing? Yeah, everywhere. Home, out in public, with my friends... it just never really stops.
Do you often feel physically restless or have trouble staying still, like when you're in meetings, sitting through appointments, or even just watching a movie?

Yeah, it’s really bad. Like, since I can’t play soccer like before, sitting around the house makes me feel like I’m literally crawling out of my skin. I just end up pacing from room to room all day. I used to burn off all that energy on the field, you know? We played in this indoor league over by the old mall. 

The turf there was awful, though. It was that fake grass stuffed with those tiny black rubber pellets. Man, those things get absolutely everywhere. You take your shoes off after a game and it’s like a pepper shaker exploded on the floor. I’d find them in my laundry, in my car, even in my bed somehow. My mom used to lose her mind trying to vacuum them up. We had this ancient Hoover vacuum that sounded like a jet engine, and it would just shoot the pellets right back out at your shins like little bullets. It terrified our dog. He'd hide under the couch for hours. He's a rescue, part golden retriever, part who-knows-what, but he is the biggest baby. If you even hold a broom, he thinks the world is ending. We tried to get him one of those thunder shirts once, but he just chewed the velcro off. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, sitting still. Yeah, like watching a movie or just being in the house, I can't do it. I just have to get up and pace.

So far, you've described difficulties with focus, impulsivity, and restlessness. Do these symptoms occur consistently across different parts of your life, like at home, in public, and when you were in school, or do they mostly happen in certain situations?

Yeah, it's pretty much always been like this, everywhere. Like, even way back in elementary school, it was the same stuff. My teachers were constantly moving my seat because I'd talk out of turn, or I'd forget my homework, or I'd just blow through worksheets and make all these careless mistakes. I remember Mrs. Gable in third grade—she put my desk right next to hers, facing the wall. 

It was this awful cinderblock wall painted that weird institutional yellow color. You know the color? It's like they wanted it to be cheerful, but it just looked like old mustard. My buddy Dave and I tried to scrape the paint off once with a paperclip to see what was underneath, but we just ended up snapping the paperclip. Dave was always doing stuff like that. He actually got suspended in middle school because he brought a stink bomb on the bus. It smelled like rotten eggs and burnt hair, and the bus driver had to pull over and let everyone out on the side of the highway. We were stuck out there for like forty-five minutes waiting for a backup bus, and it started raining. I had on this new pair of sneakers I'd saved up for, and they got completely ruined in the mud. I tried scrubbing them with a toothbrush and baking soda when I got home, but the white mesh was never the same. 

But yeah, the school stuff... it's always been there. Talking, forgetting things, rushing. It hasn't really changed, whether I'm at home or out or whatever.

The turf there was awful, though. It was that fake grass stuffed with those tiny black rubber pellets. Man, those things get absolutely everywhere. You take your shoes off after a game and it’s like a pepper shaker exploded on the floor. I’d find them in my laundry, in my car, even in my bed somehow. My mom used to lose her mind trying to vacuum them up. We had this ancient Hoover vacuum that sounded like a jet engine, and it would just shoot the pellets right back out at your shins like little bullets. It terrified our dog. He'd hide under the couch for hours. He's a rescue, part golden retriever, part who-knows-what, but he is the biggest baby. If you even hold a broom, he thinks the world is ending. We tried to get him one of those thunder shirts once, but he just chewed the velcro off. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, sitting still. Yeah, like watching a movie or just being in the house, I can't do it. I just have to get up and pace.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's symptoms are present in multiple settings, which would support a diagnosis of ADHD (F90.0) over a possible differential of another condition (e.g., F48.1/Generalized Anxiety Disorder) where symptoms may be more context-dependent.
doctor.question: So far, you've described difficulties with focus, impulsivity, and restlessness. Do these symptoms occur consistently across different parts of your life, like at home, in public, and when you were in school, or do they mostly happen in certain situations?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Even in elementary school, teachers were always moving my seat because I talked out of turn, forgot homework, and rushed through worksheets with careless mistakes.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms occurred when the patient was in school, which directly prompts the patient to discuss their childhood onset and experiences in elementary school.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it's pretty much always been like this, everywhere. Like, even way back in elementary school, it was the same stuff. My teachers were constantly moving my seat because I'd talk out of turn, or I'd forget my homework, or I'd just blow through worksheets and make all these careless mistakes. I remember Mrs. Gable in third grade—she put my desk right next to hers, facing the wall. 

It was this awful cinderblock wall painted that weird institutional yellow color. You know the color? It's like they wanted it to be cheerful, but it just looked like old mustard. My buddy Dave and I tried to scrape the paint off once with a paperclip to see what was underneath, but we just ended up snapping the paperclip. Dave was always doing stuff like that. He actually got suspended in middle school because he brought a stink bomb on the bus. It smelled like rotten eggs and burnt hair, and the bus driver had to pull over and let everyone out on the side of the highway. We were stuck out there for like forty-five minutes waiting for a backup bus, and it started raining. I had on this new pair of sneakers I'd saved up for, and they got completely ruined in the mud. I tried scrubbing them with a toothbrush and baking soda when I got home, but the white mesh was never the same. 

But yeah, the school stuff... it's always been there. Talking, forgetting things, rushing. It hasn't really changed, whether I'm at home or out or whatever.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a lifelong pattern of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity that is pervasive across multiple settings (home, school, work, public), with onset in childhood. There is significant functional impairment in occupational and organizational domains. No evidence of a single, sustained major depressive episode or exclusively situational anxiety to support F48.1.
